about: The plan (the source; PLAN.md is written from it). Edited only with node tools/plan.mjs. Dev reads it.
head:
# J Production · The World Plan

The one document of truth for the whole project: where it's going, what
holds always, every part of the world, what's being built now, what comes
next, what's parked and what's done. **Its eight parts never change** (shape
kept by `node tools/plan.mjs check`). Any request lands in one of them;
nothing ever adds another plan file. Details that *explain* how things work
live in the docs listed in part 8; they never hold plans or ticks.
chaptersIntro: *The fixed list. Every road and parked item sits under one of these.*

chapters.name: The world
chapters.what: what players see and do: the bar, avatars, games, people.
chapters.now: the bar is built and alive (three rooms, darts, chess, piano, 4K Mania, racing, bartending, jukebox, voice, profiles); the new light is live; the freeze lifted (J8.3), now remade item by item: the world remake J35, J70-J77 (every thing its own model, placed, lit and heard).

chapters.name: The site
chapters.what: the front door, the showcase, the news.
chapters.now: J Production's front page (Home, Projects, News) in Ember, with highlights pushed from Dev (R5); open again since J8.3.

chapters.name: The engine
chapters.now: Looped: E1-E9 built (things with live loops, physics, sound, net), real light L1.1-L1.7 live, the tests' own lighting (J2.4); the script language is scoped (J43, J78-J81: small, safe, errors with a line and a fix hint); open again since J8.3.

chapters.name: The tools
chapters.now: Dev (R4), the Studio, Dials, the UI Editor, Ember everywhere (R6); the five books and their checks are done (J1-J8); next: Dev remade (J90) and the Studio's Loop Maker (J57).

chapters.name: The backbone
chapters.now: accounts with ages, the ledger (credits), the multiplayer room, voice; accounts still on IONOS; both deploys report their real state to Dev (J2).

now.title: The piano redone
now.about: The piano redone: its note glow at the piano (it shows mid-room), a bigger, better keyboard to play, held pedal and pianissimo to fortissimo, songs that keep playing when you leave the bench, particles from the strings (zigzagging up, some shot far up) (request 2026-10-26 #13)

pieces.text: The piano's note glow at the piano (it showed in the middle of the room); songs keep playing when you leave the bench; pedal held through a song and real loudness from pianissimo to fortissimo
pieces.check: Play a song and stand up: it keeps playing; the glow is over the keys; quiet notes are soft, loud ones strong

pieces.text: A new, bigger keyboard to play: full width, taller keys you can see and press well, two octaves at a time that slide, the pedal and your loudness by where you press
pieces.check: Sit at the piano: the keyboard fills the bottom of the screen; press near the top for soft, near the bottom for loud

pieces.text: Particles from the strings when notes play: sparks zigzagging up and some shot far up toward the ceiling
pieces.check: Play: light rises from the strings in zigzags, some shoot high

roadIntro: *Next and later, by chapter. Every item: its job number, what it is, the North star line it serves, and its verdict (docs/playbook/intake.md step 3), judged as if unfrozen: nothing outside the freeze's list starts before J8. Old tags stay valid as "Formerly".*

world.text: Alive avatars: breathing, blinking, looking at whoever talks, shifting weight, feet planted on stairs; one body with sliders.

verdict.why: Procedural motion on the skeleton the engine already has; Claude writes it, your phone judges how alive it feels

world.text: Real people: skin light passes into, hair strands, wet see-through eyes, clothes that swing, lips that follow voice.

verdict.why: Phone speed: skin light, hair strands and swinging cloth are among the most expensive things to draw on a phone; each ships only if the frame budget allows (J37's report)

world.text: Your face: an avatar face from a few selfies.

verdict.why: Building a face from photos with no outside libraries (rule: from scratch) is research; a time-boxed try shows whether it looks like you

world.text: Memory: the floor wears where people walk, the dartboard gets holes, your usual stool gets your nameplate.

verdict.why: Wear and holes that everyone sees and that last need the room to decide and keep shared things

world.text: Mood and chance: one cozy↔wild dial for the whole bar; "maybe" events (30% rain, a surprise band).

verdict.why: The world model's states, rules and loops already cover moods and chance; a dial and events are data plus a little engine

world.text: Time and era: scrub time back and see ghosts replay the night; a "what if" copy; the era dial (1920s ↔ neon future).

verdict.why: Replaying the night needs the room to record every shared move; the room's storage is limited, so a replay keeps one night

world.text: Scale and layers: shrink to mouse size; blend two places.

verdict.why: Mouse size strains the engine's precision, light and physics; a try shows whether it holds on the phone

world.text: Home screen with "Happening now": start at your home, one tap to a busy hub, a live event or a friend.

verdict.why: It shows homes and events, so those come first

world.text: Lobbies and matchmaking: a few main hubs (the bar first), instances, matching by age band, preferences and skill; the no-friends lobby.

verdict.why: Matching by age band needs ages enforced on the server (Charter: teens and adults apart)

world.text: Your home: invite-only, placing things on a smooth grid, expand up to 3x, levels 1-3.

verdict.why: Homes others visit need the room to keep their state; invite-only rooms already exist (the room "looped")

world.text: Events and the memory book: date, time, RSVP, a clean invite card; the in-game camera, a photo book with likes, no comments, per-photo privacy.

verdict.why: Shared photos of teens need the safety tools and server-side age bands first (Charter: law and safety)

world.text: Safety in the world: teens and adults kept apart (lobbies, voice, messages); block, mute, report (keeps the last seconds of voice); the teen phrase builder, filtered text for adults.

verdict.why: Age bands and reports enforced on the server first; keeping seconds of voice for reports needs a privacy notice: your call

world.text: The mall, IKEA-style: walk in, pick things up, cart, checkout, delivery and install at home.

verdict.why: Delivery and install go to your home; buying uses earned credits through the ledger, which exists

world.text: The casino: 18+, earned credits only, never bought or cashed out.

verdict.why: 18+ enforced on the server and the safety tools in place first (Charter: the 18+ casino, earned credits only)

world.text: Small interactions done properly: bell, guitar, books, TV, door, taps.

verdict.why: Books, the TV and the taps become their own things in the world remake

world.text: Physics props: knock bottles off, glasses break and stack, pour drinks.

verdict.why: Bottles and glasses become real things first; the physics exists

world.text: The pool table.

verdict.why: A new thing with physics (balls, a cue) the engine already has; its model grown by script

world.text: Room 3, taped off today (its question is still open).

verdict.why: Waits only on your answer to its open question: what room 3 becomes (a music studio, a quiet library lounge, or something else)

world.text: Chess: bots with a chosen Elo, a menu to find a 1v1 or pick a bot.

verdict.why: A chess engine with a chosen strength, from scratch in C++, is well within reach; finding a 1v1 uses the room

world.text: Live low-res machine screens and a fair queue (20 s to claim your turn).

verdict.why: Phone speed: every live screen draws a second picture each frame; the fair queue itself is room logic and cheap

world.text: More arcade games; bots in two-player races.

verdict.why: Our own game code, like the arcade today; race bots reuse the race's AI

world.text: Racing, your plan (docs/plan/jobs/W20.md): the driving rework's stages on our own made-up makes (Vance Ridgeback GS, Kaito Sora 24, Hoshi R13 Twin, Hoshi Kaze 2.0: shapes close to the real cars, real specs, no real names or badges; your decision 2026-10-19); the rigs' screens show the driver's race so anyone in the bar can watch; and the race's visual upgrade (a real track instead of the glitchy terrain, light through the leaves, soft sun reflections, water) done together with the track rebuild in stage 14 (your answer: combine them so nothing is done twice).

verdict.why: Your plan is complete and fits the limits: made-up makes keep it legal (a lawyer checks before anything is sold), the physics is ours; the light through leaves and water cost phone speed, so they ship within the frame budget (J37's report)

world.text: Bodies that move right: stepping when turning on the spot, sit-down and stand-up motions, hands that really hold things, a face that moves when you talk.

verdict.why: Builds on the alive avatars' motion

world.text: Your own character builder (face, details); outfits and gadgets to show off (shop items).

verdict.why: The body with sliders first; outfits are sold for earned credits through the ledger

world.text: The game screens remade in Ember after R6: HUD, 4K Mania and race screens, emote faces, the loading screen.

verdict.why: Plain HTML over the 3D in the house theme (rule: the menus stay HTML), no cost on the phone

world.text: The world remake, step 7, placement: every thing sits on something real (a floor, a shelf, a table, a wall), snaps there in the Studio, and the place check refuses things floating, sunk or overlapping.

verdict.why: The place check (tools/place_check.py) and the inventory's Sits on column exist; this makes them strict

world.text: The world remake, step 8, light with the things: every lamp, bulb, sconce, neon sign and the fire is a thing that carries its own light at its real spot and bulb colour, each room balanced again (no light without a source).

verdict.why: The light rule (light only from light sources) and the light engine exist; the lights move from helper spots onto their things

world.text: The world remake, step 9, sound with the things: every thing that makes a sound carries it (the fire crackles from the fireplace, music from the speakers, glasses clink where they are), from its material's sound.

verdict.why: The sound engine and the materials' sounds exist; sources move onto their things; your phone judges how it sounds

world.text: The cozy lounge grows: a bigger fireside room that breaks normal architecture (expanded beyond the old wall, its own nooks and levels) (request 2026-10-26 #8)

verdict.why: It changes the room shell, so it comes with or after the shells' remake

world.text: A sunken seating nook by the big mirror: a few steps down, seats, a pair of speakers, its own chill music with its own player to pick and control tracks (request 2026-10-26 #8)

verdict.why: A change to the floor and walls (with the shells); music only with a licence that allows it, like the jukebox's CC-BY tracks

world.text: A holographic race broadcast in a wall recess above the sim rigs: the whole track as a spinning hologram, one camera on both drivers that splits smoothly into one per driver when they separate (one camera in solo play), the placing at the top, a minimap of the track with both cars in two colours at the bottom (request 2026-10-26 #8)

The world remake, step 6, the room shells remade: the hall, the lounge's and the arcade's walls, floors and ceilings at real size with clean edges and real materials; doors and windows become things that open

verdict.why: The props are out (J70-J73), so the shells are only walls, floors and ceilings; formerly J74's job, moved for the user's notes (2026-10-26 #12)

world.text: Books with turning pages: swipe from the left or right edge and the page curls over, its text bending with it (request 2026-10-26 #13)

verdict.why: The reader (J99) lays out pages; a page curl is drawn by the page itself (CSS 3D or canvas)

engine.text: Light leftovers: Air gets bounce strength and exposure range; the budget meter counts patches (lights in real units shipped in L1.7).

verdict.why: Small additions to the light that's live

engine.text: The engine phone check: fix every "broke" from the E1-E9 list; a ?perf=1 report by the fire with the mirror in view (against 63H3FJ, 16.7 ms); if reflections or shadows cost over 1 ms, make them cheaper.

verdict.why: Needs your phone: a ?perf=1 report by the fire; Claude can't measure the phone (Charter: Claude)

engine.text: Bug: the menu stops answering after some games.

verdict.why: GitHub's "the menu still answers after every game" passed in run 214; a try on your phone shows whether it still happens

engine.text: Speed: three phone reports (after entering, at the mirror, after 2 min walking); faster drawing part 2 (render core, layout from Blender, quality settings).

verdict.why: Three ?perf=1 reports from your phone, then the drawing work they point to

engine.text: Clean core leftovers: 4.1c, 4.3b, the darts / bartending / race adapters, entity ids on the wire.

verdict.why: Clean-up inside our own engine code

engine.text: Real surfaces: textures that never visibly repeat, rounded edges, automatic wear, dirt and smudges.

verdict.why: Phone speed and memory: textures that never repeat, and wear, cost texture memory in a browser tab; built within the budget

engine.text: Shadows and shaped light: every light casts shadows, real lamp patterns (IES), lampshades that glow, fire that moves its shadows, contact shade.

verdict.why: Phone speed: a shadow from every light costs a lot on a phone; done light by light against the frame budget (J37's report)

engine.text: The script language, step 1, its design on paper: our own small, safe language for what things do (states, events, timers, loops, remembered values, messages between things), readable by you and by AIs, every error with its line and a fix hint; the grammar on one page, 20 scripts for things that exist today, every error's words; nothing built. Its scope and jobs: docs/plan/jobs/J43.md.

verdict.why: A small language inside our own engine, from scratch in C++ (rule: no outside engines); the scope is kept small on purpose, and this step is paper only

engine.text: Eyes and camera: smooth edges (TAA), white balance like the eye, seeing in the dark, film grain in the dark, focus (no glare or starbursts: only real light, 2026-10-25 #10).

verdict.why: Phone speed: smooth edges, glare and grain are extra full-screen passes; each gets an off switch

engine.text: Layers: varnish over wood, velvet and fabric sheen, brushed metal, wet surfaces.

verdict.why: Layers sit on top of the real surfaces

engine.text: Reflections and caustics: several reflection captures, screen reflections, light bounced off shiny things, caustics.

verdict.why: Phone speed and memory: more reflection captures and screen reflections cost frame time

engine.text: The air, the rest: dust in the light, smoke near the ceiling, heat shimmer (the haze and beams come in J91).

verdict.why: Phone speed: haze and beams through the air are expensive; a cheap version first

engine.text: Recipes: stool, chair, table, bottle, glass grown from recipes, every copy slightly different, dials in the Studio.

verdict.why: Models grown from recipes by script is how Claude makes 3D (Charter: Claude); the Studio's dials show them

engine.text: Light through things and real depth: subsurface (wax, skin, lampshades), glass with thickness, parallax depth; every model at real size.

verdict.why: Phone speed: light through wax and skin, and thick glass, are expensive; every model at real size costs nothing

engine.text: Light show: theatre-style cues and light that is the music, as scripts; real bulb colours; a dying bulb.

verdict.why: Cues and light that follows the music are written as scripts

engine.text: Living light: a real sky through the windows (your time and weather), players carry light, neon afterglow.

verdict.why: Your local time is free; real weather needs an outside weather service (Charter: ask first), and a sky through the windows costs phone speed

engine.text: Scan it: bring real things in with the iPhone camera.

verdict.why: Safari gives the camera but not the depth sensor; a model from photos, from scratch, is research: a time-boxed try

engine.text: Paint the light: brush warmth and shadow in the Studio; the engine places and tunes lamps to match.

verdict.why: Working back from painted warmth to real lamps is research; a try in the Studio shows whether it's usable

engine.text: The script language, step 2, the parser and checker (C++, looped/script/): every error with its line, column, plain words and a fix hint; native tests on the 20 examples and on broken copies of them.

verdict.why: Needs the grammar settled first; plain C++ with native tests, no graphics card needed

engine.text: The script language, step 3, the tiny safe runner: events, states, timers, loops, remembered values, messages; a step budget per frame and a memory limit, a script touching only its own thing; a kind's states, rules and loops turned into a script and back without losing anything.

verdict.why: Runs inside the world model each frame; the budget keeps the phone smooth, and scripts sleep until their events

engine.text: The script language, step 4, scripts in the Studio: a script for a kind, errors underlined with their hint as you type, the change live on the phone.

verdict.why: The Studio's live editing exists; your phone judges how it is to write

engine.text: The script language, step 5, five behaviours rewritten as scripts (the light switch, the mirror, the polished things' knock, the candle, the jukebox), behaving exactly as before, the tests proving it.

verdict.why: Proves the language on real things without changing what you see

engine.text: The Loop Maker, step 1, the engine: a library of loops (patterns: sway, breathe, pulse…) used by name anywhere, and a place's timeline like a DAW's arrangement (tracks over things, clips of patterns at a beat, faded and layered on what each thing does), on the shared clock and the music's beat, the same on every phone and in the room; the showroom's stage plays a 16-beat show. Its plan: docs/plan/jobs/J85.md.

verdict.why: Our own engine code: patterns and timelines on the shared clock the world model already has

tools.text: The Studio phone check: fix every "broke S…"; a ?perf=1 report from the Studio with the Monitor open; the multiplayer test's late joiner (E3.6b) passing here too.

verdict.why: Needs your phone: every "broke S…" you report, and a ?perf=1 report with the Monitor open

tools.text: Engine flags in the Toolbelt: switch features (?light=classic, ?bounce=0 ...) without typing addresses.

verdict.why: A list of switches in the Toolbelt; no engine change

tools.text: The Loop Maker, step 2, in the Studio, like a DAW or a video editor: the timeline strip (bars and beats, playhead, play, pause, scrub, loop region, zoom), a track per thing or kind, patterns dragged on as clips (moved, stretched, faded, copied), a clip opens its pattern in the Loop Maker (lanes per channel, keys drawn with a finger, presets, saved to the library); every edit plays live and publishes for everyone. Its plan: docs/plan/jobs/J57.md.

verdict.why: The engine plays patterns and timelines first (J85); clips need no script language, only events on the timeline wait for J79

tools.text: Launch: the check (rules, overlaps, blocked doors), bot players walk the draft, a report, then Launch with one-tap undo.

verdict.why: Launch checks the timeline's draft; bot players walk it headless here (slow without a graphics card, fine for a check)

tools.text: Claude in the Studio, live: Claude's edits stream into an open Studio one by one; you comment and press Launch.

verdict.why: Claude already writes to the Studio's store with its key; the open Studio shows each edit as it lands

tools.text: The sign-up and profile browser test rewritten for the room server (tools/account_test.mjs, KI-27).

verdict.why: Our own test; sign-up and profiles have no browser test on GitHub today

tools.text: The hub's unused loop tuning (?tuning, tune) and hub/world.html's unused api() taken out (KI-29).

verdict.why: Nothing reads them since S4.2; the hub test covers what stays

backbone.text: The room checks chess moves and 4K Mania scores; then more games pay credits.

verdict.why: Touches credits, so it starts only on your yes (Charter §5); the room already runs the games' shared state

backbone.text: The room decides every shared thing (Phase 5).

verdict.why: The room (Cloudflare Durable Objects) already holds shared state; moving every shared thing there is big but within its limits

backbone.text: Safety on the server: age bands enforced, reports kept, blocks remembered.

verdict.why: Touches accounts and ages, so it starts only on your yes (Charter §5); the room and the ledger can enforce it

parkedIntro: *Not on the road yet, by chapter. The user promotes them.*

world.text: The street and the city outside; homes there as your "real home".

verdict.why: The world remake first; a city is many places, a big time cost after that

world.text: A kids edition: a separate, simpler game in the same universe (under 13).

verdict.why: The 13+ rule (2026-10-19): the platform is 13+ only, and an under-13 game brings children's privacy laws

world.text: A new name for the world and its currency (Bar3D is a working name).

verdict.why: Claude can propose names and check they're free to use; the choice is yours

world.text: Mini music studio (a DAW in the bar).

verdict.why: A big time cost: a music studio in the browser, from scratch; the sound engine exists, and room 3 could hold it (J27)

world.text: Avatar from a face scan (the user's own character builder).

verdict.why: The same research as J11 (a face from photos)

world.text: The street front: the bar seen from the street at night (front wall, lit door, people moving behind the windows, a street lamp), a new place in the world (was R5.5)

verdict.why: A new place, after the world remake

world.text: J23 · VIP marketplace (real money, its own place, unlocked forever by a first purchase; numbered, seasonal and event items) and trading (request 2026-10-24 #7: no paid services for now)

verdict.why: Needs payments (J64, parked)

site.text: The front door scene running live in Looped instead of a clip (after R6, same places).

verdict.why: Phone speed and loading: the front page would load the whole engine before showing anything; the clip below is the light way

site.text: The front page's looping clip: the camera drifting to the bar's lit door, ~8 s, rendered from the engine, behind the intro (was R5.6)

verdict.why: Drawing ~8 s of the bar here without a graphics card is very slow in the new light; a try shows whether a session can do it

engine.text: World-simulation engines: sound made from the physics, heat, smell as a field, day and night.

verdict.why: Sound from the physics, heat, and day and night are within reach; smell can only show through what you see and hear (a phone makes no smells)

engine.text: The engine checks itself: it notices when something isn't right (a thing out of place, a missing model, a broken loop) and helps say what and where (request 2026-10-24 #5)

verdict.why: Checks on the world's data and in the engine (a thing out of place, a missing model, a broken loop); the Handbook's inventory already flags some

engine.text: Smooth edges (4x MSAA, or a cheaper smoothing pass): out of J88 on the user's word, for later when we optimize; MSAA smooths jagged edges but costs phone speed and ~75 MB (request 2026-10-25 #13; research in docs/plan/jobs/J88.md)

verdict.why: Phone speed and memory: Filament rates 4x MSAA high cost on mobile

engine: Lamps sorted in 3D cells: left out after research (no gain in the bar: every lamp reaches every cell; the per-pixel cap shortens lamps, not the cells; docs/plan/jobs/J88.md)

engine.text: Bounced light at its own pace (J88.3, undone by J96): redo once the cause of its square of light is found (incident 2026-10-25-square-of-light)

verdict.why: Why pacing the bounce makes a square isn't known yet

tools.text: AI dock: a workspace on the site where you talk to Claude and it works on the project there.

verdict.why: Talking to Claude from the site needs a paid API key kept on a server (Charter: money, secrets): your decision

tools.text: AI inside the Studio (needs a paid API), importing your own models, mesh editing, several people editing at once.

verdict.why: The AI part needs a paid API (your decision); each imported model needs a licence; mesh editing and editing together are big time costs

tools.text: A design for the Studio more like a 3D modelling room (the hub card "Design idea").

verdict.why: A new look for the Studio's frame in Ember; your phone judges it

tools.text: J69 · The tests on a GitHub machine with a graphics card, so the new light is tested too (KI-28; request 2026-10-24 #7: no paid services for now)

verdict.why: GitHub's machines with a graphics card are paid; the shader check, the pictures here and your phone cover the new light meanwhile

tools.text: Claude gets better from how the user works with it: what worked, what the user liked or corrected, kept as lessons in the books and read at every session start, so the engine, the Studio and modelling get easier each time (2026-10-25 #2)

verdict.why: Claude can't be retrained, but the books can learn: lessons written from each session and read at the next (the Playbook and the records already do part of this)

tools.text: Claude gets better from how the user works with it: what worked, what the user liked or corrected, kept as lessons in the books and read at every session start, so the engine, the Studio and modelling get easier each time (2026-10-25 #2)

verdict.why: Claude can't be retrained, but the books can learn: lessons written from each session and read at the next (the Playbook and the records already do part of this)

backbone.text: The site on Cloudflare Pages (unlocks threads in the game).

verdict.why: A hosting change is your decision (Charter §5: hosting); Cloudflare Pages is free and can send the headers threads need, IONOS can't

backbone.text: J63 · Voice relays: TURN for strict networks, then a voice server (SFU) for big lobbies (request 2026-10-24 #7: no paid services for now)

verdict.why: Relays cost money per use, and there's no budget for paid services now; voice works without them on most networks

backbone.text: J64 · Payments (Stripe) for the VIP store (request 2026-10-24 #7: no paid services for now)

verdict.why: A payment provider, tax handling and terms; a provider like Stripe takes a cut of each sale rather than a monthly fee, so it can come back once there is something to sell

backbone.text: J89 (accounts hardened) is built inside J60: the new logins on Cloudflare get its expiry, guessing limit and one-at-a-time saves (request 2026-10-25 #7)

verdict.why: Folded into J60

backbone.text: J60 · Everything off IONOS (accounts, every store, the site and the bar's files to Cloudflare, then the address switch): put off, IONOS works for now (request 2026-10-25 #9); its plan stays in docs/plan/jobs/J60.md

verdict.why: On the free plan the password hashes are as strong as 10 ms per login allows; the switch needs your two changes

- `docs/archive/DECISIONS.md`: gotchas and why things are the way they are.
- `docs/archive/`: every old plan and progress file, kept to read, never to plan from.
